blockers.summary: §3.4's NCBI-chain sentence reports three numbers the instrument does not produce, attributes them to a platform the instrument never queried, and draws a causal conclusion the real numbers invert. The document prints: 'the repaired NCBI chain's own counts are concordant with both §3.2a diagnoses: 4,303 accessions queried -> 4,303 resolved to a nuccore UID (100 %) -> 59 linked to a gene. The UID step works now and returned zero before; the gene-link yield is genuinely low because these are ESTs, which is precisely why UniGene - not elink - is the right resource for them.' The artifact's only NCBI run at that scale is on GPL6244 (GSE24369) and reports ncbi_n_accessions_queried 4303, ncbi_accessions_resolved_to_a_uid 4103 (95.4 %, not 4,303 and not 100 %), ncbi_accessions_linked_to_a_gene 3163 (not 59), ncbi_genes_named 2653. The number 59 appears nowhere in the artifact. The sentence sits inside the paragraph about GSE4303 / GPL3290, where NCBI was never queried at all — that platform carries ncbi_global_budget_exhausted, which the artifact itself labels an ABSENT READING. And the stated cause is inverted twice over: 3,163 of 4,303 answered accessions (73.5 %) DID link to a gene, and GPL6244's GB_LIST holds mRNA/RefSeq accessions (BC136848, AK298283, M37726, AK074482), not ESTs. The one genuinely EST-keyed platform that was queried, GPL2937, linked 2 of 30,433 — and its own field says why: ncbi_budget_exhausted_in_elink_at 600, a truncated run, not a property of ESTs.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature.per_platform['GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz'].probe_mapping_diagnostic.{ncbi_n_accessions_queried=4303, ncbi_accessions_resolved_to_a_uid=4103, ncbi_accessions_linked_to_a_gene=3163, ncbi_genes_named=2653, ncbi_n_accessions_answered=4303, example_probe_accessions=[BC136848, AK298283, M37726, ...]} ; same file, per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].probe_mapping_diagnostic.ncbi_global_budget_exhausted = 'the cross-platform accession-bridge budget (1500s) was spent on earlier platforms, so NCBI was not queried for this one. ABSENT READING — it says nothing about whether these accessions link to a gene.' ; same file, per_platform['GSE4303-GPL2937_series_matrix.txt.gz'].probe_mapping_diagnostic.{ncbi_accessions_linked_to_a_gene=2, ncbi_budget_exhausted_in_elink_at=600} ; a regex sweep of the whole artifact for any gene/link-named field equal to 59 returns nothing.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing does, and that is the finding behind the finding. No entry in research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json names this document or its artifact, and git grep at the pin finds no test module that reads emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md for a number — the only matches are lint_readability.py and a readability-splitter test, neither of which looks at values. Regenerating the artifact, re-running with a different NCBI budget, or an editorial tidy of the sentence would all leave the three wrong numbers standing. The fix is to correct all three to 4,303 / 4,103 / 3,163, name GPL6244 as the platform they came from, delete the 'because these are ESTs' clause (it is false for GPL6244 and unsupported for GPL2937, whose low yield the artifact attributes to a spent elink budget), and state that GPL3290 — the platform carrying the verdict — was never queried.

blockers.summary: §8.2 attributes four verbatim block quotations, a sentence count, and the statement 'was fetched for exactly this comparison and its full text is open' to 'Gracilla et al., Cancer Research 2026;86:2660-2677, PMID 41811428 — the peer-reviewed version'. The producing instrument never read that paper. atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py hard-codes MECHANISM_PMID = '37205599' and fetches only that record and its PMC full text; the artifact's mechanism_paper_on_hr_deficiency block records pmid 37205599, journal 'bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology', doi 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578, year 2025, fulltext_pmcid PMC10187251. The '54 of its sentences mention HR/BRCA/PARP' is that module's n_such_sentences, computed over the preprint. I fetched the published version (PMC13223543) and checked each quoted string: none of the four appears in it. The published paper replaced 'ES' with 'Ewing sarcoma' throughout and reworded — e.g. it reads 'we nominate THE suppression of ATM activation and signaling as a new DDR lesion in EWING SARCOMA cells ... for the class of FET-REARRANGED cancers', 'in summary, these results demonstrate that TUMORS OF PATIENT WITH EWING SARCOMA do not display the genomic signatures of BRCA1/2-MUT cancers', and it split the discussion sentence into two ('We find that Ewing sarcoma tumors are not "BRCA-like" (i.e., isolated loss of HR) but rather harbor partial ATM defects. ... These data may explain the lack of clinical responses to PARP inhibitor monotherapy in patients with Ewing sarcoma'). The document's version of that last one — 'Our discovery that ES tumors are not "BRCA-like", but instead harbor partial ATM defects, may help explain ...' — exists only in the preprint. A second quoted 'sentence', 'ES patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency.', is a section HEADING in both versions, not a sentence. The scientific substance survives the version change; the provenance does not, and §8.4's whole argument turns on what this paper says in its own words.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py:109 MECHANISM_PMID = "37205599"; :299-302 grab(f"europepmc_{MECHANISM_PMID}", ...); :1200-1234 _mechanism_hr_stance writes out['pmid']=MECHANISM_PMID, out['fulltext_pmcid']=inp['mechanism_pmcid'], out['n_such_sentences']=len(uniq) with the list truncated to uniq[:40] ; research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json#mechanism_paper_on_hr_deficiency.{pmid=37205599, journal='bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology', doi=10.1101/2023.04.30.538578, fulltext_pmcid=PMC10187251, n_such_sentences=54} and #fetch_status.mechanism_fulltext_xml='HTTP 200, 156566 bytes' ; research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json#mechanism_pmcid = 'PMC10187251' ; PMC13223543 full text fetched 2026-09-01 — string search for each of the four quoted passages: two ABSENT outright, two present only after the ES->Ewing sarcoma and EWSR1-FLI1->EWSR1::FLI1 rewording.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: The reverse: the document was already edited once in exactly this place and the edit did not reach here. Its own Appendix row records 'PMID 37205599 cited for route 1's mechanism paper ... already corrected in the companion document's own reference list but not propagated here until this hardening round' — the prose citation was swapped to 41811428 while the instrument that produced the quoted text was left pointing at 37205599, so the correction created the mismatch rather than fixing it. Nothing detects it: no guard compares a quoted string in the manuscript against the artifact field it came from, and both PMIDs resolve and are clean in the retraction sweep. Either re-point MECHANISM_PMID at PMC13223543 and re-quote from the published text, or say plainly that the quotations are from the bioRxiv preprint (PMID 37205599 / PMC10187251) of the paper published as Gracilla et al. 2026 and that the published wording differs.

p1s.summary: §2.1 prints 'Cellosaurus records an 18-locus STR profile'. The producing module does not claim that: emc_atr_vulnerability.py:651 writes 'Cellosaurus STR profile present ({len(st)} loci/source lines)' — deliberately hedged, because len(st) is the length of the ST block, not a locus count. The cached record's ST block has 18 lines, of which one is the 'Source(s): Cosmic-CLP=907290; DepMap=ACH-001519; RCB=RCB0508' header and one is a duplicate D13S317 (a second allele call from a different depositor). The profile is 16 markers: 15 STR loci plus amelogenin. The document dropped the instrument's own hedge and turned 'loci/source lines' into 'locus'.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_a.cellosaurus.record.ST — 18 entries: 'Source(s): ...', Amelogenin, CSF1PO, D13S317 (x2, RCB and Cosmic-CLP/DepMap), D16S539, D18S51, D21S11, D3S1358, D5S818, D7S820, D8S1179, FGA, Penta D, Penta E, TH01, TPOX, vWA ; research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py:651.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing. The count is hand-typed prose against an unpinned artifact field, and the same '18-locus STR profile' phrasing is already replicated in research/manuscripts/surface-targets/emc-surface-target-landscape.md — so a fix here leaves a second copy. Both should read '16 markers (15 STR loci plus amelogenin)', or simply 'an STR profile cross-referenced to ...'.

p1s.summary: The Appendix states as fact that 'the preprint's identifier stopped resolving 2026-08-07 -> 2026-08-09'. PMID 37205599 resolves today: PubMed efetch returns the full bioRxiv record (PMC10187251, doi 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578), and the §8 module's own committed cache — fetched 2026-08-27, eighteen days after the stated window — carries the Europe PMC response verbatim with hitCount 1 for EXT_ID:37205599 AND SRC:MED plus a 156,566-byte PMC full text. The companion document states the same observation properly bounded ('On 2026-08-07 the query ... returned hitCount: 1 ... on 2026-08-09 the identical query returned nothing') and adds 'no claim that this identifier names nothing may be repeated'. This document drops both the date-bounding and that instruction, leaving a live manuscript asserting that a currently-resolving identifier does not resolve.
p1s.evidence: PubMed efetch for 37205599, 2026-09-01: title 'FET fusion oncoproteins disrupt physiologic DNA repair...', bioRxiv, PMC10187251 ; research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json#europepmc_37205599 = '{"version":"6.9","hitCount":1,..."pmid":"37205599","pmcid":"PMC10187251"...}' with atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json#fetched_utc = 2026-08-27T04:35:40Z ; research/manuscripts/citation-retraction-sweep.json#records['PMID:37205599'] = {status: clean, via: PubMed esearch [uid], 2026-09-01} ; contrast research/manuscripts/dependency/emc-atr-collaborator-package.md:551.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Time already did. A transient Europe PMC indexing gap was written into the appendix as a durable property of the identifier, and the module that would have contradicted it re-fetched the same identifier successfully three weeks later without anything comparing the two. Rewrite as the companion does: a dated Europe PMC observation on two named days, with the note that the identifier resolves at PubMed.

p1s.summary: §2.2 prints '~5-11 % of EMC carries no identified FET partner' with no citation, and there is no source for it anywhere in the repository. git grep at the pin finds the figure in exactly two places: this sentence, and the same module's own limits string in emc_atr_vulnerability.py:2351 (copied into the artifact). It is an epidemiological statement about a human disease used to bound a load-bearing negative — it is what keeps §2.2 from reading as a reclassification of H-EMC-SS — and CLAUDE.md §7 requires everything clinical to be cited. A sibling paper's review backlog already carries this exact gap as an open item ('§3 fusion-negative EMC, uncited. Attach one of the already-retrieved sources').
p1s.evidence: git grep -n -i -E '5[-–]11 ?%|no identified FET partner' at 20d33f34 returns only research/manuscripts/dependency/emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md:197, research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py:2351 and research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature._limits[3]; no citation map entry, no PMID, no DOI anywhere near any of them ; research/manuscripts/aso/review-backlog-2026-08-19.md:182.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing — lint_claims scores claim STRENGTH, and this sentence is correctly hedged ('~', 'a real category'); it cannot see that the number has no source. The repository's own backlog says a source has already been retrieved for the sibling paper; attaching it here and in _limits[3] closes both.

p1s.summary: Every decision rule the verdicts turn on is undisclosed. §3.4 says 'Three DDR concepts clear the raw threshold' and §6.1 grades on it, but the threshold is a hard-coded mean delta > 0.2 with no significance requirement — which is why HALLMARK DNA Repair at delta +0.178 / t 3.33 does not count as elevated while adipogenesis at +0.218 / t 5.08 does. The 'signature is DDR-specific' predicate additionally requires at most ONE unrelated control set to be elevated (signature_specific_to_DDR = bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1); the document never says so. §4's 'fraction dependent' column is computed against DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD = -0.5, which the document also never prints. The document is emphatic that the GRADING was fixed before the numbers and reproduces it verbatim — but the operationalisation that turns measurements into those grades is nowhere in the text, so a reader cannot tell whether a 0.19 delta or a 0.21 delta produced the tier.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py:2308-2321 (ddr_up_raw / ddr_up_adj / ctrl_up / prolif_up each gated on mean_delta_across_readable_platforms > 0.2), :2322 (signature_specific_to_DDR = bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1), :76 and :2448 (DEPENDENT_THRESHOLD, value -0.5 in emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_c_coordinated_dependency.dependent_threshold) ; emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_b_emc_tumour_signature.pooled_raw_contrast.control_generic_DNA_repair = {delta 0.1778, t 3.329} vs .control_adipogenesis = {delta 0.2183, t 5.081}.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Changing 0.2 to 0.15 would put replication stress into ddr_concepts_elevated_raw and changing it to 0.25 would drop ATR-CHK1 out of it, in both cases silently — the document would print a different sentence with no visible cause, and no guard ties the constant to the prose. One clause in §1 naming all three constants, or a footnote in §3.4 and §4, fixes it.

p1s.summary: §5 reports the held-out FET-fusion signature's design in half. The document says it was 'Built only on lines with no GDSC data (34 FET, 928 non-FET) and scored on the 965 lines that have it — so the correlation is not circular by construction'. The artifact carries a second caveat the document drops: the signature is 'derived from the columns this run actually read (the gene-set members plus a seeded random background sample), NOT from the whole transcriptome — so it is a signature of that subspace and is reported [as such]'. It is 100 up and 100 down genes selected from roughly 2,500 background columns plus the gene-set members, not a transcriptome-wide FET signature. The line-holdout defends against circularity; nothing defends against the subspace, and the document reports rho = -0.138 from this instrument as though it were a signature of the transcriptome.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_d_drug_response_correlation.fet_signature.{n_holdout_FET_lines=34, n_holdout_non_FET_lines=928, n_lines_with_drug_data=965, n_up_genes=100, n_down_genes=100, _caveat='derived from the columns this run actually read ... NOT from the whole transcriptome'} and .expression_scores_meta.n_background_columns_for_centering = 2500.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Nothing — the test FAILS, so dropping the caveat does not flatter the conclusion and no reviewer would look. It still matters: the row is one of four pre-registered tests and its failure is quoted in §6.1's predicate table, and a predictor built on a 2,500-column subspace is a weaker instrument than the sentence implies. One clause: '100 up / 100 down genes over the gene-set members plus a seeded ~2,500-column background sample, so a signature of that subspace rather than of the transcriptome'.

p1s.summary: The top banner states an unqualified universal negative — 'no ATR inhibitor has ever been put on an NR4A3-fusion-positive cell' — where §6.2 states the same thing correctly scoped, 'in any public dataset'. The document's own §8 then cites PMID 41651400, whose abstract says the authors pharmacotyped patient-derived cell models and tested ATRi/WEE1i/PARP1/2i combinations, and whose deposit contains an EMC-labelled patient-derived model (GSM9037837 / USZ-23_EMC3). Whether that model was in the pharmacotyping panel is UNKNOWN — the paper is paywalled and §8.2 Q1 correctly says the response data is not in the deposit — and whether it carries the fusion is also UNKNOWN (§8.3). So the claim is not refuted, but it is no longer safely universal, and the banner asserts about the world what §6.2 asserts about public data.
p1s.evidence: PubMed abstract of PMID 41651400 (Planas-Paz et al., Cancer Lett 2026;642:218300, doi 10.1016/j.canlet.2026.218300): 'By pharmacotyping patient-derived cell models, we identified promising drug targets within the DNA damage response (DDR) for sarcoma with HRD traits. Inhibition of ATR, CHK1 and WEE1 elicited synthetic lethality...' ; research/modalities/atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json#cohort_composition.members.patient_derived_cell_models['extraskelletal myxoid chondrosarcoma'] = [GSM9037837/USZ-23_EMC3] ; the document's own §8.2 Q1 and §8.3.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: The paywall lifting, or a supplementary table naming the panel. Give the banner §6.2's scope — 'in any public dataset' — and the sentence becomes true under every resolution.

p2s.summary: §3.2 lists HALLMARK 'DNA Repair' among the UNRELATED controls, beside Myogenesis, Adipogenesis and Oxidative Phosphorylation. A DNA-repair gene set is not unrelated to a DDR hypothesis; the module's own key for it is control_generic_DNA_repair, which is the honest name. It scored raw delta +0.178 (t 3.33) on GSE4303/GPL3290 — larger than three of the six DDR concepts the document does print — and it appears nowhere in §3.4's table. Nothing turns on it (it does not clear the 0.2 cut, and it collapses to -0.005 after the proliferation adjustment, which supports the paper's reading), but a reader is told four unrelated controls were run and shown two.

The primary source behind §2's central finding was not read, and the document does not say so. Cellosaurus's caution on CVCL_1238 cites PubMed=34413129 — Gartrell et al., Mol Cancer Ther 2021;20(11):2151-2165, 'SLFN11 is Widely Expressed in Pediatric Sarcoma...'. I fetched its open full text (PMC8571037): it names H-EMC-SS exactly once, in a cell-line-source list, and states 'Translocation status was confirmed using PCR and Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)' for the 14-line panel — but the words 'myxoid' and 'chondrosarcoma' do not appear in the retrievable body at all, so the datum behind the caution sits in a table or supplement I could not retrieve. The chain (document -> Cellosaurus -> 34413129) is plausible and unfalsified, and the document quotes Cellosaurus rather than the paper, which is the correct attribution. But §2 is called 'the most consequential finding in the document' and rests on a curator's reading of a source nobody in this repository has opened.
p2s.evidence: PMC8571037 full text, 2026-09-01: single H-EMC-SS mention in the cell-line provenance list (European Collection of Authenticated Cell Cultures, RRID:CVCL_1238), zero occurrences of 'myxoid' or 'chondrosarcoma', 3 of 'EWSR1' all about EWSR1-FLI1 in Ewing lines ; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json#part_a.cellosaurus.fusion_mentions_verbatim (the caution, matching the document's quote character for character).

p2s.summary: Nothing binds any number in this manuscript to its producing artifact. research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json contains no entry naming emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md or emc-atr-vulnerability.json, and git grep at the pin finds no test module that reads the manuscript for a value — the only two Python files that mention it are lint_readability.py and test_the_readability_splitter_breaks_where_a_sentence_does.py, and both look at sentence shape, not at numbers. That is the mechanism by which the first blocker's three wrong values survived a document that otherwise pins and cross-checks everything.
